title: Continuous Ingest Resilience: Queue Coordinator and Transactional Replay for Console Metrics
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: The current console metrics ingest pipeline occasionally experiences prolonged pauses and duplicate enrichment work during consumer group rebalances and partial region outages. These incidents increase downstream alert noise, raise per-token processing cost, and sometimes push latency spikes beyond SLOs for dashboard updates.

Goal: Implement a 'Queue Coordinator' component plus transactional replay semantics to: (1) minimize outage window during consumer failures/rebalances, (2) provide deterministic replay with at-most-once commit semantics for stateful enrichers, (3) expose fine-grained backpressure and priority lanes for high-SLO customers, and (4) make recovery actions observable and automatable from Console.

High-level approach:
- Introduce a Queue Coordinator service that manages partition assignments, lease heartbeats, and graceful handoff between stream processor instances. Coordinator maintains small durable manifests for each partition (owner, last-committed-offset, ephemeral-cache-checkpoint) in an S3-compatible checkpoint store plus a lightweight indexed manifest in Postgres for fast lookups.
- Add transactional replay primitives to stream processors: a replay mode that replays a contiguous offset range while keeping an idempotency window using event_ids and sequence numbers enforced by a dedupe cache (hot KV with TTL).
- Implement prioritized lanes: critical (P0 customer SLO), normal, and low (sampled) lanes. The Queue Coordinator enforces global token buckets and dynamically adjusts lane sampling rates based on queue depth and latency SLOs.
- Backpressure & graceful degradation: when queue depth or processing lag exceeds soft thresholds, the coordinator signals ingress to reduce non-essential metadata, enable aggressive sampling on low lanes, and divert non-critical enrichments to async batch paths.
- Observability: add per-partition metrics (lease age, commit-lag, replay-in-progress), end-to-end tracing headers to correlate ingress -> queue -> enrichment -> sink, and Console dashboard with lineage for replay runs.

Trade-offs considered:
- Exactly-once vs at-most-once: we prefer deterministic at-most-once for stateful enrichers (idempotent validators and counters) to avoid complex two-phase commits. We accept rare duplicates for stateless aggregations and surface them to downstream consumers via a 'replay note'.
- Checkpoint store choices: Postgres-only provides fast writes but makes large manifests expensive; S3-compatible object manifests are inexpensive and durable. We combine both for fast-path lookups + durable archive.
- Complexity: Coordinator adds orchestration overhead. To manage risk, we will roll out to a single region and single tenant pool, validate, then expand rollout automation.
acceptance_criteria: Queue Coordinator deployed to staging and managing partition leases for the staging topic with automatic failover under instance termination
Transactional replay mode can replay an arbitrary offset range for a partition with deduplication confirmed by end-to-end integration tests
Under a synthetic 10x burst test, prioritized lanes keep 95th percentile dashboard-update tail latency < 2s for P0 customers while sampled lane latency may be degraded
No long-running duplicate enrichment jobs after consumer rebalance in the controlled failure tests (duplicate rate < 0.1% for stateful enrichers)
Dashboards for per-partition lease_age, commit_lag, replay_status, and coordinator health visible in Console; alerts wired to oncall for lease-loss > 30s
A GitHub PR with code, unit tests, and integration harness merged and a canary rollout completed to a single availability zone without customer impact
